newsitem.title: FRANCE: French Socialists plan to stick to euro timetable.
newsitem.headline: French Socialists plan to stick to euro timetable.

text.p: French Socialist Elisabeth Guigou, tipped to serve as European Affairs Minister in Lionel Jospin's new government, said on Tuesday that it would stick to the timetable for Europe's planned single currency.
Asked whether the new government would seek to ensure the euro currency is created at the planned deadline of January 1, 1999, Guigou told RTL radio: "Of course we must respect this deadline."
She added that the Maastricht Treaty on criteria for economic and monetary union must be filled out, with a separate chapter on employment.

"The treaty must be completed on certain points. Institutions must be reformed to enable Europe to decide and to be more democratic...In the name of the European left, I suggested at the intergovernmental conference (IGC on institutional reform) that there be a chapter on jobs," she said.
Jospin formally takes over power from defeated Prime Minister Alain Juppe at 11 a.m. (0900 GMT) on Tuesday and will appoint his cabinet in the next 48 hours, aides said.

Jospin was appointed on Monday by President Jacques Chirac who unwittingly precipitated the move when he called a snap parliamentary election aimed at consolidating his own hold on power five weeks ago.
The Communist Party, which Jospin needs for an outright majority, has pressed for relaxation of national budget criteria set for joining the euro.
